mainTopic: Does a כהן have ownership rights (זכייה) in an unblemished בכור while the בית המקדש stands? Challenges to רב נחמן's position
overview: This amud continues the discussion of רב נחמן's view that a כהן has no ownership rights (זכייה) in an unblemished בכור while the בית המקדש stands. First, a ברייתא saying a בכור 'may be sold' is used against him. The גמרא answers that the selling refers to a blemished animal and the offering to an unblemished one. Next, רב משרשיא brings a משנה about a כהנת's child mixed up with her maidservant's child. The גמרא answers, in two versions, that the משנה is about today: these possible כהנים may keep their blemished בכור instead of giving it to another כהן. Then a ברייתא about עיר הנדחת is brought, and the גמרא answers that it is about a blemished בכור. Such a בכור is not eaten like ordinary animals, as a משנה in בכורות shows. Finally, a ברייתא that compares a בכור to שלמים as the owner's property seems to prove that a כהן owns even an unblemished בכור. The answer to this comes on the next amud.

steps.title: A ברייתא says a בכור may be sold, and it must be talking about Temple times
steps.stepSummary: An objection is raised from a ברייתא that says a בכור cannot be redeemed but can be sold. The גמרא first proves that the ברייתא is talking about the time when the בית המקדש stands.
steps.simpleTranslation: He challenged him: About a firstborn the Torah says 'you shall not redeem,' but it may be sold. What time period is this talking about? If you say nowadays, look at the end of the פסוק: 'and you shall sprinkle their blood on the altar.' Is there an altar nowadays? So it must be talking about when the בית המקדש is standing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to challenge רב נחמן. Before making the challenge, it pins down that the ברייתא is about the time of the בית המקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says a בכור 'is sold,' which suggests the כהן owns it. To make this a real challenge, the גמרא must show that the case is in Temple times, because that is when רב נחמן says the כהן has no rights. The mention of sprinkling blood on the מזבח proves the Temple must be standing.

keyTerms.meaning: A firstborn male kosher animal, which is given to a כהן
'You shall not redeem': a בכור cannot be exchanged for money to make it non-holy
'What case are we dealing with?' The גמרא asks this to pin down the exact situation
'Say the end part': look at the later part of the text to decide the case
Nowadays, after the בית המקדש was destroyed

phrases.english: He raised an objection to him:
Regarding a firstborn it is stated: 'you shall not redeem'
but it may be sold.
With what are we dealing?
If you say it is nowadays,
then look at the latter part:
'and you shall sprinkle their blood on the altar.'
Is there an altar nowadays?

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא פְּשִׁיטָא בִּזְמַן שֶׁבֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ קַיָּים.
phrases.english: Rather, it is obvious that it is when the Temple is standing.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ: בִּבְכוֹר נֶאֱמַר ״לֹא תִפְדֶּה״ וְנִמְכָּר הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב נחמן's earlier statement, which comes before this section
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's view that a כהן has no ownership rights in an unblemished בכור while the בית המקדש stands
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Builds the first half of the challenge by showing that the ברייתא's 'it may be sold' applies in Temple times

steps.title: The ברייתא must refer to an unblemished animal, so the כהן has ownership
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proves the ברייתא is about an unblemished בכור, since the פסוק talks about offering it. The ברייתא still says it may be sold, so the כהן must have ownership rights.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what kind of animal is this? If you say a blemished one, look at the end: 'sprinkle their blood on the altar and burn their fat.' Is a blemished animal fit to be offered? So it must be an unblemished one. And the ברייתא says it may be sold. This shows the כהן has ownership rights in it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the challenge. The ברייתא is about an unblemished בכור in Temple times, and it says the animal can be sold. That goes against רב נחמן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A blemished animal cannot go on the מזבח. Since the פסוק talks about offering the blood and fat, the animal must be unblemished (תם). Selling something only makes sense if you own it, so the כהן must have זכייה even in an unblemished בכור during Temple times.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal with a physical blemish, which cannot be offered as a קרבן
An unblemished animal, fit to be offered
Offering on the מזבח
'Evidently': it introduces the conclusion drawn from the source
Ownership rights, the right to acquire and own something

steps.whyThisMatters: If the כהן owns even an unblemished בכור, he could sell it or give it away. That directly contradicts רב נחמן.

phrases.english: And with what kind of animal?
If you say a blemished animal,
then look at the latter part:
'and you shall sprinkle their blood on the altar
and burn their fat.'
Is it fit for offering?!
Rather, is it not about an unblemished animal?
And it teaches that it may be sold.

phrases.aramaic: אַלְמָא אִית לְהוּ לְכֹהֵן זְכִיָּיה בְּגַוֵּיהּ!
phrases.english: Evidently, the priest has ownership rights in it!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבְמַאי? אִילֵימָא בְּבַעַל מוּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge begun in step 1 by identifying the animal as unblemished
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's view that a כהן has no ownership in an unblemished בכור in Temple times
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא covers Temple times and an unblemished animal, yet it allows selling, which implies ownership.

steps.title: The two parts of the ruling refer to different animals
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the beginning (selling) is about a blemished animal, and the end of the פסוק (offering) is about an unblemished one.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that a real proof? The first part is about a blemished animal, and the last part is about an unblemished one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב נחמן. You cannot assume both parts are talking about the same animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed that 'it may be sold' and 'sprinkle their blood' describe one animal. The answer splits them. Selling applies to a blemished בכור, which the כהן does own. Offering applies to an unblemished one, which he cannot sell. So רב נחמן's view stands.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Is that comparable?' It rejects the assumption that two parts must follow the same case
The first part of a source
The latter part of a source

steps.whatToRemember: The challenge from the ברייתא is answered. 'It may be sold' refers only to a blemished בכור. An unblemished בכור in Temple times is offered and is not sold.

phrases.english: Are they comparable?
phrases.notes: He's asking: who says both parts are talking about the same animal?

phrases.english: The first part is about a blemished animal,
the latter part is about an unblemished one.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִידֵּי אִירְיָא? רֵישָׁא — בְּבַעַל מוּם, סֵיפָא — בְּתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of steps 1-2
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the source: the beginning and end refer to different cases
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both 'it may be sold' and the offering refer to the same unblemished animal
steps.terutzMaskana: Selling refers to a blemished בכור, and offering refers to an unblemished one, so there is no proof against רב נחמן

steps.title: רב משרשיא quotes a משנה about mixed-up children
steps.stepSummary: רב משרשיא begins a new challenge. He quotes a משנה about a כהנת's child mixed up with her maidservant's child, which includes a ruling about their firstborn animals.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב משרשיא challenged: A כהנת whose child got mixed up with her maidservant's child: when the mixed-up children grow up, they free each other. Both eat תרומה, and they get one share at the threshing floor. Their firstborn animals must graze until they get a blemish, and then they are eaten with their blemish.
steps.whatsHappening: רב משרשיא starts a new challenge by quoting a משנה. This step only sets up the source. The challenge itself comes in steps 5-6.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two children are in doubt: one is a כהן and one is a slave of a כהן. Each frees the other, so whoever is the slave becomes free. Both may eat תרומה, since a כהן and a כהן's slave both may. They get only one share, because a slave gets no share of his own. Their בכורות are not offered right away but wait until they become blemished. The גמרא will next show how this ruling bears on רב נחמן's view.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who is the daughter or wife of a כהן
A maidservant (female slave)
Things (here, children) that got mixed up and cannot be told apart
They set free (from slavery)
The portion of produce given to כהנים
They become blemished and unfit to be offered

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the whole challenge yet. Here the גמרא is only quoting the משנה. The point against רב נחמן is drawn in the next lines.

phrases.english: Rav Mesharshiyya raised an objection:
A priestess whose child got mixed up
with her maidservant's child:
once the mixed-up children have grown up,
they free each other,
and both of them eat תרומה,
and they receive one share at the threshing floor.
Their firstborn animals must graze until they become blemished,
and they are eaten with their blemish.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵתִיב רַב מְשַׁרְשְׁיָא: כֹּהֶנֶת שֶׁנִּתְעָרֵבה וְלָדָהּ בִּוְלַד שִׁפְחָתָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first challenge was answered, a new challenge opens from a different source
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's view on a כהן's ownership of an unblemished בכור
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Sets up the משנה's ruling about the firstborn animals, which the גמרא analyzes in steps 5-6

steps.title: Which time period is the משנה talking about?
steps.stepSummary: רב משרשיא asks what era the משנה means. He argues it cannot be today, because then there would be no difference between the בכורות of the uncertain children and our own.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we dealing with? If you say it means nowadays, how are our בכורות different from theirs? Ours also need a blemish before they can be eaten!
steps.whatsHappening: רב משרשיא starts to pin down which time period the משנה is about. He is setting up his proof by ruling out the present day first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nowadays there is no בית המקדש, so every בכור, even a regular ישראל's, must wait for a blemish before it can be eaten. So if the משנה meant nowadays, there would be no reason to single out the uncertain children's animals. This pushes us toward the time of the בית המקדש.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with?
Nowadays, when there is no בית המקדש
Ours (a regular ישראל's) / theirs (the uncertain children's)
Blemishes that make an animal unfit for a קרבן

phrases.english: With what are we dealing?
phrases.notes: He means: which time period is the משנה from step 4 talking about?

phrases.english: If you say it is in the present time,
what is different about ours
and what is different about theirs?
Ours also need blemishes!

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן? אִילֵימָא בִּזְמַן הַזֶּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רב משרשיא's challenge by working out the setting of the משנה he quoted.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that the משנה could be about the present day.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Nowadays all בכורות need a blemish, so the משנה's special ruling for the uncertain children would add nothing.

steps.title: So the כהן must own an unblemished בכור
steps.stepSummary: If the משנה is about the time of the בית המקדש, it lets the uncertain owners keep an unblemished בכור. That only makes sense if a כהן owns it. Otherwise the Temple treasurer should take it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, isn't it talking about when the בית המקדש stands? That works if a כהן has ownership in it. But if he doesn't, let the Temple treasurer come and take it!
steps.whatsHappening: רב משרשיא finishes his challenge. Since the משנה is about Temple times, it shows that a כהן owns an unblemished בכור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Temple times an unblemished בכור should be brought as a קרבן. If the כהן had no ownership in it, the גזבר would simply take it for the מקדש. The fact that the owners keep it until it gets a blemish suggests the כהן's ownership is real.

keyTerms.meaning: Ownership rights
Treasurer of the בית המקדש
Granted, that works
Fine, it makes sense

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא לָאו בִּזְמַן שֶׁבֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ קַיָּים?
phrases.english: Rather, is it not when the Temple is standing?
Granted, if you say
the priest has ownership in it,
it is fine.
But if you say he does not have it,
let the treasurer come and take it!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לָאו בִּזְמַן שֶׁבֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ קַיָּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from step 5's point that the משנה must be about Temple times.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that a כהן has no ownership in an unblemished בכור.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the כהן had no ownership, the גזבר would take the animal. Since the owners keep it, the כהן must own it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the core proof attempt about whether a כהן truly owns a בכור during Temple times.

steps.title: The משנה is about today, and the uncertain children can keep their בכור
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה really is about nowadays. There is still a difference: a ישראל must give a blemished בכור to a כהן, but the uncertain children may each be partly a כהן, so they keep it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, it is about nowadays. And as for your question, how are ours different from theirs: we have to give it to a כהן once it is blemished. But they, since each might partly be a כהן, can push away the claims of the כהנים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof. It says the משנה is about today and shows what makes these cases special.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nowadays a ישראל still has to hand his blemished בכור to a כהן. The uncertain children are different: each might be the כהנת's son, and that possibility is enough to block any other כהן from claiming the animal. So the משנה teaches something new even for today, and nothing is proven about Temple times.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, in fact (used to keep the original reading)
Partly a כהן, a possible כהן
Removes, pushes away a claim

phrases.english: Actually, it is in the present time.
And as for what is difficult for you:

phrases.aramaic: מַאי שְׁנָא דִּידַן וּמַאי שְׁנָא דִּידְהוּ?
phrases.english: What is different about ours and what is different about theirs?
We give it to a priest once it is blemished;

phrases.aramaic: אִינְהוּ — כֵּיוָן דְּאִיכָּא בְּהוּ מִקְצָת כֹּהֵן,
phrases.english: they, since there is part of a priest in them,
it pushes away the claims of the priests.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְעוֹלָם בִּזְמַן הַזֶּה, וּדְקָא קַשְׁיָא לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב משרשיא's challenge from steps 5-6 by putting the משנה back in the present day.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-setting the case: the משנה is about nowadays, and the difference concerns who keeps the blemished animal.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה had to be about Temple times, because nowadays all בכורות are treated the same.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even nowadays there is a difference: a ישראל gives his blemished בכור to a כהן, while a possible כהן keeps his.
steps.whatToRemember: First version: the משנה is about today, and its point is that the uncertain children keep their blemished בכור instead of giving it to a כהן.

steps.title: Second version: why would the משנה single out the uncertain cases?
steps.stepSummary: In another version, the challenge goes: if the משנה is about today, why mention these uncertain cases? Even our בכורות have to graze until they get a blemish. So it must be about Temple times.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another version: If it is nowadays, why speak specifically about the בכורות of these uncertain cases? Even ours should graze! Rather, it is obviously about when the בית המקדש stands.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a second telling of רב משרשיא's challenge. It first argues again that the משנה must be about Temple times.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This version focuses on the משנה's words 'they should graze.' Nowadays every בכור has to graze until it gets a blemish, so saying it about the uncertain cases teaches nothing. That points to Temple times.

keyTerms.meaning: Another version of the discussion
Why specifically this case?
Uncertain cases (here, children of unclear parentage)
They should graze, meaning left alone until they get a blemish

phrases.english: Another version:
If it is in the present time, why specifically
the firstborns of these uncertain ones?
Even ours should also graze!

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא פְּשִׁיטָא בִּזְמַן שֶׁבֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ קַיָּים,
phrases.english: Rather, it is obvious it is when the Temple is standing.

steps.triggerLanguage: לִישָּׁנָא אַחֲרִינָא: בִּזְמַן הַזֶּה, מַאי אִירְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Restarts רב משרשיא's challenge in a different version, which focuses on the word 'graze.'
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that the משנה is about the present day.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Nowadays all בכורות graze until they get a blemish, so the משנה would have no reason to single out the uncertain cases.

steps.title: It must be an unblemished animal, which shows it can normally be sold
steps.stepSummary: The animal cannot be blemished, since the משנה says it grazes until it gets a blemish. So it is unblemished, and only in this uncertain case may it not be sold. That implies a definite כהן can sell it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if it is about a blemished animal, how can it say 'graze until they get a blemish'? They are already blemished! Rather, it is obviously about unblemished animals, and only in a case like this can they definitely not be sold.
steps.whatsHappening: The second version finishes its challenge. It shows the משנה is about an unblemished בכור and draws a conclusion about selling it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'until they get a blemish' only makes sense if the animal is now unblemished. The גמרא reads the משנה as saying that only these uncertain owners may not sell it. That suggests a definite כהן may sell an unblemished בכור in Temple times, which would prove he owns it.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal with a blemish
They become unfit for a קרבן (by getting a blemish)
Unblemished animals
They sell

phrases.english: And if it is about a blemished animal,
would it say 'they should graze until they become unfit'?
They are already unfit!
Rather, it is obviously about unblemished ones,
and it is only in a case like this that they definitely do not sell.
phrases.notes: The hint is that a definite כהן could sell even an unblemished בכור.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי בְּבַעַל מוּם — יִרְעוּ עַד שֶׁיִּסְתָּאֲבוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the second version of the challenge started in step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that a כהן has no ownership in an unblemished בכור.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה blocks a sale only in the uncertain case, which implies a definite כהן may sell an unblemished בכור, and that means he owns it.

steps.title: Second answer: today, the uncertain children can turn the כהן away
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers again that the משנה is about nowadays. A ישראל cannot turn a כהן away from his בכור, but each uncertain child can say 'I am a כהן,' so they keep it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, it is about nowadays. What bothers you, that even ours should graze? We cannot turn the כהן away, because there is no possible כהונה here. These uncertain ones can turn the כהן away: each one says to the כהן, 'I am a כהן,' 'I am a כהן.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the present-day reading against the second version of the challenge. It explains the special point of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ישראל has no claim to כהונה, so he must give the בכור to a כהן. Each uncertain child can claim to be a כהן himself, so no outside כהן can take the animal from him. The משנה's point is about who keeps the animal today, so it proves nothing about Temple times or about selling.

keyTerms.meaning: We push away, we turn someone away
A possible claim to being a כהן

steps.whatToRemember: In both versions the answer is the same: the משנה is about today, and it teaches that a possible כהן may keep his בכור. So it does not prove that a כהן owns an unblemished בכור in Temple times.

phrases.english: Actually, it is in the present time.
What is difficult for you,
that even ours should also graze?
We are not able to turn away the priest,
phrases.notes: Some versions have מצינו (in round brackets); the corrected wording, in square brackets, is מצינן. Both mean 'we are able.'

phrases.english: since there is no possible priesthood here.
These uncertain ones can turn away the priest:

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל חַד וְחַד אָמַר לֵיהּ לְכֹהֵן:
phrases.english: each one says to the priest:
'I am a priest,' and 'I am a priest.'

steps.triggerLanguage: לְעוֹלָם בִּזְמַן הַזֶּה, מַאי קַשְׁיָא לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the second version of the challenge from steps 8-9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-setting the case: the משנה is about nowadays and is about pushing away an outside כהן's claim.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'They should graze' teaches nothing new for today, so the משנה must be about Temple times and unblemished animals.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even today the ruling is new: a ישראל must give his בכור to a כהן, but the uncertain children can claim to be כהנים and keep it.

steps.title: A teaching about the destroyed city is brought as a challenge
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי שמעון: "בְּהֶמְתָּהּ" leaves out the בכור and מעשר animals in an עיר הנדחת, and "שְׁלָלָהּ" leaves out the מעשר שני money in it.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: רבי שמעון says: "its animals" leaves out the firstborn and tithe animals in the city. "Its spoil" leaves out the second-tithe money in the city.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to challenge the earlier discussion. This step only quotes the source; the next steps will show why it is a problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah says that when an עיר הנדחת is destroyed, its animals and its spoil must be destroyed. רבי שמעון reads two words as exclusions: "בְּהֶמְתָּהּ" leaves out holy animals, and "שְׁלָלָהּ" leaves out holy money. The גמרא will now ask which word excludes the בכור, and what that tells us.

keyTerms.meaning: A city whose people mostly worshipped idols. The city and its property are destroyed.
A firstborn kosher animal, which is given to a כהן
The animal tithe, every tenth animal, which is holy
The second tithe. It, or the money that redeems it, is eaten or spent in ירושלים.
"Its spoil," the city's property that must be burned

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
Rabbi Shimon says:
"Its animals"
phrases.notes: דברים 13:16, about destroying the עיר הנדחת.

phrases.english: excludes firstborn and tithe animals that are in it;
"Its spoil"
excludes second-tithe money that is in it.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new outside source into the question of whether a כהן owns an unblemished בכור.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that a כהן has no ownership (זכייה) in an unblemished בכור in Temple times
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Setup only. The force of the challenge is developed in steps 12–13.

steps.title: The teaching must be about Temple times
steps.stepSummary: An עיר הנדחת can only be declared by the court of 71, so the ברייתא must be about the time when the בית המקדש stood.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case is this? If it is nowadays, can there even be an עיר הנדחת? We learned that only a court of 71 can declare a city an עיר הנדחת. So it is clearly about the time when the בית המקדש stood.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what time period the ברייתא describes, and answers that it must be Temple times.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עיר הנדחת needs the great סנהדרין of 71 judges, and that court does not exist today. So the ברייתא must describe Temple times. In Temple times, the question of whether a כהן owns an unblemished בכור really matters.

keyTerms.meaning: "What case are we dealing with?"
Nowadays, when there is no בית המקדש
The great סנהדרין of 71 judges
"It is obvious"

phrases.english: With what are we dealing?
If you say nowadays,
is there such a thing as an idolatrous city?
But we learned in a Mishnah: one does not declare an idolatrous city
phrases.notes: This משנה is the start of מסכת סנהדרין.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא בְּבֵית דִּין שֶׁל שִׁבְעִים וְאֶחָד!
phrases.english: except by a court of seventy-one!
Rather, it is obvious
that it is when the Temple is standing.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן? אִילֵימָא בִּזְמַן הַזֶּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the time period of the ברייתא quoted in step 11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the ברייתא about nowadays or about Temple times?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Temple times, because an עיר הנדחת needs a court of 71.

steps.title: Why use "its animals" unless the כהן owns it?
steps.stepSummary: A blemished בכור would be included in "בְּהֶמְתָּהּ", so the ברייתא must mean an unblemished one. If the כהן did not own it, it should be excluded from "שְׁלָלָהּ", which leaves out Heaven's property.
steps.simpleTranslation: What kind of בכור is it? If it is a blemished one, that counts as "its animals"! So it is clearly an unblemished one. If a כהן owns it, the verse fits well. But if he does not own it, why do we need "its animals"? It should be excluded from "its spoil," which means the city's spoil and not Heaven's.
steps.whatsHappening: Here the גמרא makes the real challenge. The way the ברייתא excludes the בכור seems to prove that a כהן owns an unblemished בכור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A blemished בכור belongs to the כהן like any animal, so it should be destroyed as "בְּהֶמְתָּהּ". That means the ברייתא must be talking about an unblemished בכור. If nobody owned it, it would be Heaven's property and "שְׁלָלָהּ" would already exclude it. The ברייתא needs "בְּהֶמְתָּהּ" to exclude it, which suggests it is someone's property, the כהן's.

keyTerms.meaning: A blemished animal, which cannot be offered
An unblemished animal, fit to be offered
Ownership rights
"Derive it instead from…"
"Heaven's spoil," holy property that belongs to Heaven

steps.confusionAlert: Both words exclude things, but in different ways. "שְׁלָלָהּ" leaves out property that belongs to Heaven. "בְּהֶמְתָּהּ" would only be needed for an animal that belongs to a person, here the כהן.

phrases.english: And in what case? If we say a blemished animal,
that is "its animals"!
phrases.notes: A blemished בכור belongs to the כהן, so it should be destroyed along with the city's animals.

phrases.english: Rather, it is obviously an unblemished one.
Granted, if you say
that he has ownership in it, that is fine;
but if you say he does not have it,
why do I need it from "animals"?
Derive it from "its spoil,"
and not the spoil of Heaven!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבְמַאי? אִי נֵימָא בְּבַעַל מוּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the Temple-times setting to complete the challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that a כהן has no ownership (זכייה) in an unblemished בכור in Temple times
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: "שְׁלָלָהּ" already excludes Heaven's property. Since the ברייתא needs "בְּהֶמְתָּהּ" for the בכור, the בכור must be private property, meaning the כהן owns it.

steps.title: It is a blemished בכור, which is not eaten like an ordinary animal
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא is about a blemished בכור. "בְּהֶמְתָּהּ" only means animals eaten like ordinary animals, so it leaves out the בכור and מעשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, it is about a blemished animal. As for your problem that it should count as "its animals": "its animals" means animals eaten the ordinary way. That leaves out the בכור and מעשר, which are not eaten like ordinary animals.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא is about a blemished בכור, and explains why it is still not included in "בְּהֶמְתָּהּ".
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even after it gets a blemish, a בכור or מעשר keeps special rules and is not eaten like a plain animal. So "בְּהֶמְתָּהּ" does not include it, and the ברייתא is not talking about an unblemished בכור at all. That means it gives no proof that a כהן owns an unblemished בכור.

keyTerms.meaning: "Really," used to keep the original reading and reject the challenge
Eaten in the ordinary way the city's animals are eaten
"And as for what bothered you"

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא about עיר הנדחת is about a blemished בכור. A blemished בכור or מעשר is not "בְּהֶמְתָּהּ" because it is not eaten like ordinary animals, so the ברייתא proves nothing about whether a כהן owns an unblemished בכור.

phrases.english: Actually, it is about a blemished animal,
and as for what was difficult for you,
that this is "its animals":
"its animals" means what is eaten as ordinary "its animals,"
which leaves out firstborn and tithe,
which are not eaten as "its animals."
phrases.notes: Some versions say "not included in" (the words in round brackets); the corrected wording, in square brackets, reads "are not eaten as."

steps.triggerLanguage: לְעוֹלָם בְּבַעַל מוּם, וּדְקָא קַשְׁיָא לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 13 by redefining the word "בְּהֶמְתָּהּ".
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the verse's word, so the case becomes a blemished animal
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A blemished בכור counts as "בְּהֶמְתָּהּ", so the ברייתא must be about an unblemished one.
steps.terutzMaskana: "בְּהֶמְתָּהּ" only includes animals eaten the ordinary way. A blemished בכור or מעשר is left out, so there is no proof of the כהן's ownership.

steps.title: A blemished בכור and מעשר are not sold like ordinary meat
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a משנה as support. Most disqualified קדשים may be sold and weighed in the butchers' market like ordinary meat, but a בכור and מעשר may not.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: All disqualified consecrated animals are sold in the butchers' market, slaughtered in the butchers' market, and weighed by the ליטרא. The exceptions are the בכור and the מעשר, because the benefit from them goes to the owners.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is backing up the last step. It shows from a משנה that a blemished בכור and מעשר are not eaten like ordinary animals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 14 said that "בְּהֶמְתָּהּ" only covers animals eaten like ordinary animals. This משנה proves that a בכור and מעשר are treated differently: they cannot be sold in the market or weighed by the pound. So they really are left out of "בְּהֶמְתָּהּ".

keyTerms.meaning: Consecrated animals that became disqualified, for example by a blemish, and were redeemed
The butchers' market
A litra, a unit of weight; meat sold by the pound like ordinary meat
Their benefit goes to the owners, not to the הקדש

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that even a blemished בכור keeps special limits, which is why "בְּהֶמְתָּהּ" leaves it out. With that, the challenge from עיר הנדחת is answered.

phrases.english: As we learned in a משנה: All disqualified consecrated animals
are sold in the butchers' market,
and are slaughtered in the butchers' market,
and are weighed by the litra,
except for the firstborn and the tithe animal,
since their benefit goes to the owners.
phrases.notes: When the money goes to הקדש, a higher market price is allowed. Here the owner gains, so that reason does not apply.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies a משנה proving step 14's claim that a בכור and מעשר are not eaten like ordinary animals.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that a blemished בכור and מעשר are not treated like ordinary animals, so "בְּהֶמְתָּהּ" leaves them out.
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in בכורות: a בכור and מעשר may not be sold in the market or weighed by the litra, unlike other disqualified קדשים.

steps.title: A ברייתא about lying under oath over קדשים owned by someone else
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with three opinions. They disagree about which קדשים count as the owner's money for the law of falsely denying someone's property. One opinion says this applies only to a בכור.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged from a ברייתא: "And commits a trespass against ה׳" comes to include קדשים קלים, since they are the owner's money. These are the words of רבי יוסי הגלילי. בן עזאי says: it comes to include שלמים. אבא יוסי בן דוסאי says: בן עזאי only said this about a בכור.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new challenge. It quotes a ברייתא that seems to treat a בכור as the owner's own money. The full attack has not been made yet; this step lays out the source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק talks about a person who falsely denies holding his friend's property. The ברייתא says this law also covers certain קדשים, because they count as the owner's money. According to אבא יוסי בן דוסאי, בן עזאי applied this to a בכור, so a בכור belongs to its owner. That may clash with what was said earlier about who owns a בכור.

keyTerms.meaning: "And commits a trespass against ה׳", from the פסוק about falsely denying a friend's property
To include; the פסוק adds another case
Offerings of lesser holiness, whose meat the owner may eat
The owner's own money or property
Peace offerings

steps.confusionAlert: This is not about מעילה, the misuse of הקדש. The פסוק is about lying under oath to deny holding someone else's property. The question is whether קדשים count as that person's property.

phrases.english: They raised an objection: "And commits a trespass against the Lord" —
phrases.notes: ויקרא 5:21. The פסוק is about someone who swears falsely that he does not have his friend's deposit.

phrases.english: this comes to include offerings of lesser sanctity,
since they are the owner's property,
these are the words of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili.
Ben Azzai says: it comes to include peace offerings.
Abba Yosei ben Dosai says:
Ben Azzai did not say this
except with regard to a firstborn alone.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי: ״וּמָעֲלָה מַעַל בַּה׳״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the support in step 15, the גמרא brings a new ברייתא as a challenge on whether a בכור is its owner's property.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's view that a כהן has no ownership (זכייה) in an unblemished בכור while the בית המקדש stands
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא, as explained by אבא יוסי בן דוסאי, treats a בכור as the owner's money. The exact problem is spelled out after the גמרא fixes the time period.

steps.title: The ברייתא must be about the time of the בית המקדש
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which era the ברייתא is about. It cannot mean nowadays, because it compares a בכור to שלמים. So it must mean when the בית המקדש stood.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we dealing with? If you say it is nowadays, the ברייתא teaches the בכור as similar to שלמים! Rather, it is obvious that it is about the time when the בית המקדש stands.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pins down the time period of the ברייתא before pressing its challenge. This sets up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שלמים can only be brought when the בית המקדש is standing. Since the ברייתא puts a בכור side by side with שלמים, it must be talking about that same time. So the challenge is about a בכור in the days of the בית המקדש, which is often an unblemished one fit for an offering.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with?
If you say...
Nowadays, when there is no בית המקדש
Similar to; taught alongside
It is obvious

phrases.english: With what are we dealing?
If we say it is in the present time —
but it teaches it as similar to peace offerings!
phrases.notes: שלמים are only brought when there is a בית המקדש, so the comparison would make no sense nowadays.

phrases.english: Rather, it is obvious
that it is when the Temple is standing.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן? אִילֵימָא בִּזְמַן הַזֶּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Clarifies the time period of the ברייתא from step 16 so the challenge can be pressed.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the ברייתא talking about nowadays or about the time of the בית המקדש?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Since it compares a בכור to שלמים, it must be about the time when the בית המקדש stood.

steps.title: What kind of בכור is the ברייתא talking about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what case the ברייתא is about: a blemished בכור or an unblemished one.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what case are we dealing with?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks what kind of בכור the ברייתא means. This sets up the next move, where it will test each option.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 17 already settled that the ברייתא is about the time of the בית המקדש. Now the open question is the animal's condition: בעל מום (blemished) or תם (unblemished). The answer will decide whether the ברייתא proves the כהן owns even an unblemished בכור.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with? A question that asks for the exact situation.
A firstborn male animal, which is given to a כהן.
The owner's money, meaning property that truly belongs to its owner.

phrases.english: And with what are we dealing?
phrases.notes: He means which kind of בכור the ברייתא from step 16 is talking about.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבְמַאי עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on step 17, which fixed the era. Now the גמרא narrows down the type of animal.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the ברייתא talking about a blemished בכור or an unblemished one?

steps.title: It cannot mean a blemished בכור, because it is compared to שלמים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries saying the ברייתא means a blemished בכור, then rejects this because the ברייתא puts the בכור side by side with שלמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it means a blemished animal, that cannot be, because the ברייתא teaches the בכור as being like שלמים!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the first option, that the ברייתא means a blemished בכור, and pushes it away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שלמים belong to their owners even while they are unblemished and fit to be brought. The ברייתא treats the בכור the same way as שלמים, so it must mean a בכור in that same state, which is unblemished. Saying the ברייתא means a blemished בכור would break that comparison.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say. This brings up a possible answer that is about to be rejected.
An animal with a blemish, which cannot be brought on the מזבח.
Similar to, or parallel with.
Peace offerings, which belong to their owners.
It teaches. This points to what the ברייתא says.

phrases.english: If you say it is about a blemished animal —
but it teaches it as similar to שלמים!
phrases.notes: שלמים belong to the owner even when unblemished, so a בכור compared to them should be unblemished too.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵימָא בְּבַעַל מוּם הָא דּוּמְיָא דִּשְׁלָמִים קָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the challenge by ruling out the first option.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects reading the ברייתא as talking about a blemished בכור.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: That reading does not fit the ברייתא's comparison of the בכור to שלמים, which are owned even when unblemished.

steps.title: So the ברייתא means an unblemished בכור, and the כהן owns it
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא must be talking about an unblemished בכור. This proves the כהן has real ownership of it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, is it not about an unblemished animal? Learn from this that the כהן has ownership of it.
steps.whatsHappening: Once the blemished option is out, the גמרא concludes that the ברייתא means an unblemished בכור. From this it draws its proof that the כהן owns it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא calls the בכור the owner's money, and we now know it means an unblemished בכור. So even an unblemished בכור counts as the כהן's property. This is the payoff of the challenge that began in step 16, and it goes against רב נחמן's view that a כהן has no ownership in an unblemished בכור while the בית המקדש stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, is it not...? This introduces the only option left.
An unblemished animal.
Learn from it. This marks a conclusion drawn from a source.
Right of acquisition, meaning ownership.
In it, here meaning in the בכור.

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא treats a בכור like שלמים, so it must mean an unblemished בכור. That seems to show the כהן owns an unblemished בכור while the בית המקדש stands.
steps.whyThisMatters: This conclusion attacks רב נחמן's position that an unblemished בכור is not the כהן's property, so his view will need to respond to it.

phrases.english: Rather, is it not about an unblemished animal?
And learn from it
that the כהן has ownership in it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לָאו בְּתָם וּשְׁמַע מִינַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: With the blemished option ruled out in step 19, the גמרא lands on the unblemished option and draws its proof.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The ברייתא seems to prove that a כהן has real ownership of an unblemished בכור while the בית המקדש stands. This challenges רב נחמן's view.
